review_candidates.description: # 회사 소개 팩타고라는 AI의 신뢰 계층(Trust Layer)을 만듭니다. 지금의 AI 에이전트는 "무엇이 맞는지"는 찾지만 "언제 맞았는지"는 모릅니다. 법과 규칙이 바뀌어도, 어제 맞았던 답을 오늘도 그대로 말합니다. 팩타고라는 사실과 판단을 시간과 인과로 기록하는 에이전트 메모리를 만듭니다. 그래서 AI가 시점에 맞는 답을 하고, 그 근거까지 보여줄 수 있습니다. 핵심 엔진은 오픈소스(FactBlock)로 공개하고, 규칙이 계속 바뀌는 전문 산업을 첫 시장으로 삼고 있습니다. # 포지션 소개 팩타고라의 CBDO는 영업 담당자가 아닙니다. 기술을 매출로 바꾸는 경로를 설계하고, 한국 팀을 이끄는 리더입니다. 우리는 법무(Legal)와 세무(Tax) 분야에서 첫 고객 파일럿을 시작했습니다. CBDO는 이 첫 사례를 반복 가능한 판매 방식으로 만들고, 정부 사업으로 성장 자원을 확보합니다. 대표가 해외에 있는 동안에는 한국 팀의 목표와 요구사항을 정하고, 진행 상황을 관리하며, 약속한 결과가 나오도록 책임집니다. 대표와 함께 무엇을 팔지, 누구에게 팔지, 얼마에 팔지를 결정하고, 그 결과는 계약, 매출, 사업 수주로 확인됩니다. # 담당업무 **사업개발과 영업** - 법무, 세무 분야 첫 고객 파일럿을 유료 계약으로 전환하고 레퍼런스 사례로 만들기 - 로펌, 회계법인, 관련 SaaS를 대상으로 영업 파이프라인 구축과 직접 세일즈 - 가격 모델과 파일럿 구조(범위, 기간, 성공 기준) 설계 - 디자인 파트너와 전략 파트너 발굴 및 계약 - 오픈소스(FactBlock) 사용자를 유료 고객으로 전환하는 경로 설계 **정부 사업** - 정부 과제와 공공 사업 기회 발굴, 우선순위 판단 - 사업계획서 작성과 제안, 발표 대응 - 수주한 과제의 일정, 산출물, 보고 관리와 기관 커뮤니케이션 **팀 운영 (대표 부재 시 한국 팀 리드)** - 회사 우선순위에 맞춰 팀원별 목표와 요구사항 정의 - 주간 진행 상황 점검, 막힌 일 해결, 일정 조정 - 대표와 정기 공유, 주요 결정 사항 보고 - 고객 요구를 제품 로드맵으로 연결해 엔지니어링 팀과 우선순위 협의 **투자와 대외** - 투자 유치(IR) 자료와 피칭에서 시장과 매출 전략 담당 # 자격요건 - B2B 사업개발, 엔터프라이즈 세일즈, 파트너십 리드 경험 7년 이상 - 초기 단계 제품으로 첫 유료 고객을 직접 만들어 본 경험 - 정부 과제 또는 공공 사업을 기획, 제안, 수행해 본 경험 - 팀을 이끌며 목표 설정과 진행 관리를 해 본 경험 - 기술 제품(AI, 데이터, SaaS, API)을 고객 언어로 설명할 수 있는 분 - 한국어, 영어 모두 비즈니스 수준 # 우대사항 - 법률, 회계, 세무, 금융 등 규제가 많은 전문 산업 대상 영업 경험 - TIPS, 중기부, 과기정통부, NIPA, IITP 등 정부 지원사업 수주 경험 - 엔지니어 중심 조직을 관리해 본 경험 - AI, LLM, RAG, 에이전트 시스템에 대한 이해 - 미국 시장 B2B 세일즈 또는 파트너십 경험 - 스타트업 창업 또는 초기 멤버(Pre-Seed ~ Series A) 경험 - 투자 유치 과정에 참여한 경험 # 이런 분을 찾고 있습니다 - 회의보다 고객 미팅을 먼저 잡는 분 - "좋은 기술"보다 "고객이 돈을 내는 이유"를 먼저 묻는 분 - 팀에 "열심히"가 아니라 "무엇을 언제까지"를 요구할 수 있는 분 - 정해진 플레이북이 없어도 직접 만들어 가는 분 - AI를 활용해 더 빠르게 일하는 방법을 고민하는 분 - 신뢰할 수 있는 AI와 정보 환경을 만든다는 팩타고라의 미션에 공감하는 분 # 처우 - 경력과 역량에 따라 협의 - 스톡옵션 (협의) --- 🚩 채용 프로세스 서류접수 → 1차 면접 (대표 면접, 사업 과제 발표) → 최종합격

review_candidates.title: Certification Specialist - Software and/or AEH and/or Systems Development Assurance (DA)
review_candidates.description: Job description: (5658) Certification Specialist – Software and/or AEH and/or Systems Development Assurance (DA) (Internally this role is titled “Design and Certification Specialist”) Starting Salary: up to £72,000, plus a Market Related supplement (MRS) Contract Type: Permanent, Full-time Location: Gatwick / Hybrid Required Security Level: SC Visa Restrictions: This position does not currently offer visa sponsorship. Closing Date: 08 Nov 2026 Interview Date: WC 23 Nov in person Gatwick We are the UK's aviation and aerospace regulator and recognised as a world leader in its field. Our activities are diverse, enabling the aviation industry to meet the highest safety standards, and we pride ourselves on our ability to adapt to the constantly evolving aviation environment. The Role As a Software and/or Certification Airborne Electronic Hardware (AEH) and/or Development Assurance (DA) Engineer, you will be responsible for supporting the overall business plan and supporting the wider CAA, specifically in establishing and delivering the UK’s ICAO State of Design responsibilities. Reporting to the Design & Certification Principal Specialist for Avionics, Electrical Systems & Development Assurance, you will be accountable for the technical investigation/analysis and approval of certification projects and the continued airworthiness of aircraft, systems, engines and propellers, across all civil aerospace domains including commercial air transport, general aviation, certified unmanned air vehicles and innovation projects. This is a varied role that will include significant interaction with industry representatives both remotely and in person. It will also involve the review and approval of new parts and products and their design changes, validation of other nations’ certifying authorities’ work as well as the investigation of the UK Design Organisations’ design approvals. Industry and regulatory engagement will be required to ensure that the CAA keeps appraised of future projects, the proposed introduction and development of new and innovative technologies and any proposed regulatory changes Core Accountabilities 1. Personal Accountabilities Promote a safety and learning culture that is risk based but also satisfies our basic statutory and international needs including compliance. Act in accordance with the CAA’s HR policies, applying our values and behaviours policies in their day-to-day role. Actively contribute to Personal Development Conversations, including future personal development and progression opportunities. Create time to learn and develop. Ensure that all recommendations and decisions are proportionate to the needs and safety expectations of the sector and are consistent with extant regulatory policy (using objective risk assessment techniques as necessary) 2. Design and Certification Accountabilities Evaluate certification projects, as directed by the Principal Design and Certification Specialist, in relation to aerospace products. These may include submissions from both UK Design Organisations and those provided for validation under bilateral arrangements. Determine compliance with airworthiness requirements and making recommendations for approval of product or change through sampling of submitted applicant data in accordance with Level of Involvement principles. Support applications for Flight Conditions, using your specialist knowledge and skills to make a recommendation whether an air or rotorcraft meets the intent of ‘safe flight and landing’ in lieu of full or partial certification compliance. Ensure that aerospace products, for which the CAA has responsibility, meet applicable initial and continued airworthiness standards and ensure in-service issues are adequately addressed to maintain the intended level of safety. Additionally, play a leading role in the development of associated airworthiness requirements. Clarify, where necessary, existing airworthiness requirements and contribute to the development of new requirements to cover new technology, novel applications of existing technology, and novel proposals for compliance demonstration (this could be through authoring Certification Review Items, as appropriate). Enact type design liaison responsibilities on aerospace products and make recommendations as appropriate to colleagues inside and outside CAA (including other Regulatory Agencies) to ensure continued airworthiness and safety standards are met. When required, act as Project Certification Manager (PCM) to coordinate projects or ‘specialists’ in specific technical disciplines. Identify and coordinate research or contribute into areas of significant airworthiness concern. Represent the CAA and / or Airworthiness in decision making committees and working groups, internally and externally, nationally and internationally from a design standpoint. Liaise with other regulators and accident investigation bodies in relation to accidents and events and their ICAO Annex 13 investigations or equivalent. About You: Ideally, you will be able to demonstrate industry experience with an equivalent qualification, be a proven expert with detailed knowledge of the functioning and management of the aerospace industry, and have proven aerospace experience, preferably working for an approved aerospace organisation. Essential Criteria: Proven knowledge of certification of highly complex systems and their development and integration, Software and/or Airborne Electronic Hardware (AEH) and/or Aircraft System Certification, with experience in performing Stage of Involvement Audits (SOI) and/or System Reviews (SRs) with regulatory bodies. This could have been gained from working within Industry as an expert and/or gained through relevant experience within an Airworthiness Authority. We anticipate you will have demonstrable knowledge and experience in one or more of the following technical areas: Software up to IDAL A Knowledge of IMA design and architecture Familiarity with avionics communications protocols including ARINC, AFDX and serial interfaces. Familiarity with single core and multi-core certification requirements Experienced with software and hardware integration and formal verification methods Well versed in procedural and Object orientated programming languages. Hands-on experience (preferably leading) SOI audits. Airborne Electronic Hardware (AEH) up to IDAL A Experience in applying and following the guidance of ED-80/DO-254 at various Item Design Assurance Levels (IDALs). Hands-on experience of Hardware Architectures and design processes related to hardware RAM/Flash Based FPGAs, ASICs, COTS processor/devices, PDH. Familiarity with avionics communications protocols including ARINC, AFDX and serial interfaces. Hands-on experience (preferably leading) SOI audits. Experience in verification methods, RTL, Post-Layout, Hardware integration. Experience with Advanced Verification Methods is a plus. A process-oriented mindset, but with the capability to assess technically complex hardware and certification aspects for AEH Development Assurance (DA) up to FDAL A Experience in defining the scope of and leading System Reviews per ARP4754A/B for various Functional Development Assurance Levels (FDALs) Familiarisation with various safety analysis techniques per ARP4761 and how they are applied to derive safety objectives. The ability to review and analyse aircraft, system, sub-system and item architectures with respect to safety objectives (including a good understanding of the decomposition of Functional to Item Development Assurance Levels). An understanding of system life‑cycle processes. Confidence in critiquing proposed requirements analysis, decomposition and traceability. Experience in managing interfaces and ensure cross‑discipline consistency – decomposition through indenture levels from aircraft to items. You will also be: Able to operate in various cultural business environments at all levels. Capable of using experience and making sound judgments. Able to think laterally to identify any wider implications. Able to effectively manage your own workload with a wide variety of projects with differing priorities. Able to understand specialist issues and modulate technical views to account for wider business and political considerations. Able to challenge information, propositions or assumptions, often of a deep technical nature and across a range of disciplines, affecting safety. Capable of making timely, reasoned decisions. Able to decide when enough information is available to make a decision affecting safety. Able to identify when to escalate issues to their Line Manager and others as appropriate. Confident communicator at all levels, having the ability to conduct technical conversation and engage with all stakeholders. Able to perform report writing and co-ordination of reports in support of your day-to-day role. Capable of using multiple IT systems and infrastructure in order to fulfil the objectives of your day-to-day role. Able to act in a professional and collaborative manner with both internal and external stakeholders. Desirable Criteria: The desire to continually develop experience through project involvement and dedicated training. Experience in design/development assurance of Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Travel: There will be UK and international travel required to perform SOI and/or SR activities and for other purposes dependent on business requirements. Additional Information: For many appointments within the CAA, these roles require access to operationally sensitive infrastructure and/or Nationally Protected information. For these roles the post holders must undergo National Security Vetting and achieve the appropriate level of clearance. To be vetted we will usually expect a reasonable period of residency in the UK so that meaningful checks can be undertaken. For this role this will need to be 5 years. If you do not meet these requirements, we may not be able to accept your application. For more information on CTC and SC clearance please visit - Vetting explained - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk) The CAA is committed to maintaining the highest standards of integrity, professionalism, and ethical conduct. To help ensure transparency and protect the independence and reputation of the CAA, candidates invited to interview will be required to complete a Declaration of Interests form, disclosing any actual, potential, or perceived conflicts of interest that could influence, or be seen to influence, their ability to perform the role objectively and impartially. Relocation & Property The CAA will be relocating from Aviation House (Our Gatwick Office) to new premises in a few years’ time. Our move is driven by strategic, operational and environmental considerations. We will be moving to a new local home, up to a 15-mile radius of Aviation House, to minimise disruption for our valued colleagues and customers. We are now working with colleagues and visitors to understand what we need in our new office, before we start our property search. We will sell Aviation House and land, vacate the site and move to new premises, but we do not expect to move before 2028 Inclusive Recruitment We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome applications from all backgrounds. As a Disability Confident employer, candidates who meet the minimum requirements will be guaranteed an interview. Find out more about the Disability Confident Scheme. If you require any adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know. Use of Artificial Intelligence by candidates in the CAA recruitment process We recognise that many of our candidates find Artificial Intelligence to be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be rejected on that basis. Working With Us Explore What We Offer section on our careers website to find out about our benefits and how we support work-life balance. Our Values Do The Right Thing, Never Stop Learning, Build Collaborative Relationships, Respect Everyone – For more information please Click Here Closing Date: 08 Nov 2026 Interview Date: WC 23 Nov in person Gatwick We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. Therefore, if you are interested, please submit your application as early as possible. No recruitment agencies please.
